items.title: Doc2Harness: Benchmarking LLMs on Long-Horizon Harness Engineering of Coding Agents
items.content: Agents driven by large language models are increasingly deployed on long-horizon tasks, where they use tools and modify real workspaces. How well they perform depends as much on the harness around the model as on the model itself. Existing benchmarks measure downstream task success under a fixed harness, leaving harness engineering itself unexplored. We propose Doc2Harness, a two-stage benchmark that evaluates long-horizon harness engineering directly. In Stage 1, a build model operating inside
items.author: HF Daily Papers
items.summary: An arXiv paper proposing Doc2Harness, a two-stage benchmark for evaluating long-horizon harness engineering for coding agents. It argues that agent performance depends as much on the harness around the model as on the model itself, and that existing benchmarks only measure downstream task success under a fixed harness. Stage 1 involves a build model operating inside a workspace to construct or improve the harness, with later stages evaluating the resulting harness.
items.reasoning: Directly relevant to agent harness design, a core concern for Hermes Agent-style systems. Introduces a novel evaluation methodology rather than a new model, giving it solid technical depth, but it is a research paper without immediate product impact.

items.content: Self-distillation in agentic reinforcement learning has produced a growing number of methods. items.author: HF Daily Papers
items.summary: A reality-check paper on self-distillation methods in agentic reinforcement learning. It finds that existing evaluations often reuse published baseline scores under inconsistent experimental conditions, offer few direct comparisons between contemporaneous methods, and under-examine training stability and computational cost. items.title: Any Time, Any Space: A World-State-Centric Framework for Agentic Video Generation
items.content: Long-form agentic video generation must turn a screenplay into shots that remain spatially and temporally consistent across nonconsecutive requests. items.author: HF Daily Papers
items.summary: A paper presenting ATAS, a world-state-centric framework for long-form agentic video generation. It compiles a screenplay into shot requests with explicit location, camera, and event-time references, and retrieves relevant world-state information before generation to keep shots spatially and temporally consistent across nonconsecutive requests, going beyond passing prompts or recent frames.
items.reasoning: Technically interesting in video generation and state tracking, but tangential to Hermes Agent workloads and terminal/coding agent ecosystems; limited cross-relevance except conceptually for shared agent state.

items.title: Show HN: I built a Claude Code plugin to query 10.6M earnings-call embeddings
items.content:
Hi HN,

I've been using LLMs for one-off market questions against a database of earnings transcripts since ~2025. In tech years that's a long time so as a Solo dev I built a platform around it and have been adding miscellaneous other financial tools and integrations. Backend infrastructure is super boring! PostgreSQL & ElasticSearch, with the data appropriately sharded and replicated across two regions.

Some example requests:

"What did NVIDIA say about data-center demand
